texts.preamble: Gujarat Co-Operative Milk Marketing ... vs Adjudicating Officer/Joint ... on 6 April, 2026 Author: Bharati Dangre Bench: Bharati Dangre Nisha 2026:Bhc-Os:8593-Db Digitally signed by Nisha Sandeep Sandeep Chitnis Date: 2026.04.08 Chitnis 16:02:23 +0530 23-wpl In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Ordinary Original Civil Jurisdiction Writ Petition No.387 Of 2023 Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation Limited
texts.facts: 2. On 4th January 2020, the Food and Drugs Administration, Mumbai carried out raid in the godowns of the petitioner and seized 23-wpl.387.2023.doc huge quantity of product called "Amul Lite" and "Delicious." Since the goods were seized, which allegedly were in contravention of the Food Safety and Standards Regulations which according to the petitioner were not yet finalized and had not yet come into force and therefore the seizure of the products according to the petitioner was unjustified. 3. When the petitioner approached this Court, he raised a challenge to the impugned action and sought release of the products with permission to market the same after repackaging them in conformity with the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Gujarat Co-Operative Milk Marketing ... vs Adjudicating Officer/Joint ... on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183231633/ 2 An alternative prayer was also sought that the seized products may be permitted to be sent back to the manufacturing unit for utilization as non-human consumption and as far as the product "Delicious." is concerned, it upon been blended @ 10% in the existing recipe, which would take care of the sub-standard parameters, it shall be packed in revised packaging material and then sold in the open market. Apart from this, challenge was also raised to the amendment/modification under the Food Safety and Standards 23-wpl.387.2023.doc (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018, by declaring that it is illegal, ultra vires and contrary to the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. A declaration was also sought that the said Regulations of 2018 had not yet come into force on the date when the action was initiated against the petitioner and its goods came to be seized. 4. Upon the petition being filed, on 5 th November 2020, the Division Bench of this Court, taking note of the submissions advanced on behalf of the State Authorities, since it was indicated that it is going ahead with the auction, the goods being perishable in nature and State had already issued notices and tenders have been received, did not grant any interim relief. However, as far as the prayer of the petitioner for initiating any coercive action, the order directed that if the respondents-authorities intend to take any coercive steps they will give 15 days advance notice to the petitioner. The order also directed that any amount recovered through the sale conducted by the State Government will be subject to 23-wpl.387.2023.doc further orders to be passed in the petition. 5. The interim order granted to the aforesaid effect continued to remain in force and today when the writ petition is called up for hearing, learned counsel Mr. Khandeparkar made a categorical statement that he is not pressing for the challenge to the validity of the amended Regulation of 2018. By inviting our attention to the affidavit-in-reply filed by the Assistant Commissioner (Foods) on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 5, raising a preliminary objection that the petitioner had not availed any statutory remedy of Appeal available under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, and therefore the petition need not be entertained.
texts.arguments: Mr. Khandeparkar make a statement that if the Appeals are directed to be decided within a time bound manner, as the product has now been analyzed and the report was submitted by the Food Analyst, but it had not yet attained finality in the wake of pendency of the Appeals, the petition would serve its purpose as the further course of action available to the petitioner as well as to the department would be only considered subsequent to the adjudication of the pending Appeals. 6.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Mr. Khandeparkar make a statement that if the Appeals are directed to be decided within a time bound manner, as the product has now been analyzed and the report was submitted by the Food Analyst, but it had not yet attained finality in the wake of pendency of the Appeals, the petition would serve its purpose as the further course of action available to the petitioner as well as to the department would be only considered subsequent to the adjudication of the pending Appeals. 6.
